subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the relative charge of a proton?
questions.explain: Protons carry a relative charge of +1.

questions.q: How is the mass number of an atom calculated?
questions.explain: Mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons.

questions.q: Which flame colour indicates the presence of sodium ions?
questions.explain: Sodium ions produce a yellow flame in a flame test.

questions.q: Why is the relative mass of an electron taken as very small?
options: An electron's mass is negligible compared with a proton or neutron
questions.explain: An electron's mass is about 1/1836 of a proton's, so it is treated as negligible.

questions.q: Adding sodium hydroxide to iron(III) ions produces a precipitate that is:
questions.explain: Iron(III) ions give a brown precipitate of iron(III) hydroxide.

questions.q: Potassium ions produce which colour in a flame test?
questions.explain: Potassium ions give a lilac flame colour.

questions.q: Which technique would best separate a soluble solid from its solution to obtain crystals?
questions.explain: Crystallisation evaporates the solvent so the dissolved solid forms crystals.

questions.q: Which statement about a mixture is correct?
options: It always has a fixed composition
It can only be separated by chemical reactions
Its substances are not chemically combined and keep their properties
Its substances are chemically bonded together
questions.explain: In a mixture the substances are not chemically joined, so they can be separated by physical means.

questions.q: Boron exists as 20% boron-10 and 80% boron-11. What is its relative atomic mass?
A pure substance, unlike a mixture, will:
options: Melt and boil at specific sharp temperatures
Melt over a range of temperatures
questions.explain: A pure substance has a sharp, specific melting and boiling point, whereas mixtures melt and boil over a range.

questions.q: What is the approximate relative mass of an electron compared with a proton?
questions.explain: An electron's mass is negligible, roughly 1/1836 of a proton's.

questions.q: What is the electronic structure of magnesium (12 electrons)?
questions.explain: Filling 2 then 8 then 2 gives 2,8,2 for 12 electrons.

questions.q: Copper ions produce which colour in a flame test?
questions.explain: Copper ions give a green flame colour.

questions.q: When silver nitrate is added to a bromide solution, the precipitate formed is:
questions.explain: Bromide ions form a cream precipitate of silver bromide.

questions.q: Calcium ions give which colour in a flame test?
questions.explain: Calcium ions produce an orange-red flame.

questions.q: Which test confirms that a gas is hydrogen?
options: It gives a squeaky pop with a lit splint
questions.explain: Hydrogen produces a squeaky pop when a lit splint is held to it.

questions.q: What is the relative charge of a neutron?
questions.explain: Neutrons are electrically neutral, with a relative charge of 0.

questions.q: The atomic number of an element tells you the number of:
questions.explain: The atomic number equals the number of protons in the nucleus.

questions.q: A white precipitate forms when barium chloride is added to a solution containing:
questions.explain: Sulfate ions form a white precipitate of barium sulfate with barium chloride.

questions.q: In paper chromatography, the Rf value is calculated as:
options: Distance moved by solvent - distance moved by substance
Distance moved by solvent / distance moved by substance
Distance moved by substance x distance moved by solvent
Distance moved by substance / distance moved by solvent
questions.explain: Rf = distance moved by the substance divided by the distance moved by the solvent.

questions.q: Which subatomic particle is found outside the nucleus?
questions.explain: Electrons occupy shells (energy levels) outside the nucleus.

questions.q: Which scientist proposed that electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed energy shells?
questions.explain: Bohr suggested electrons occupy fixed shells (energy levels) around the nucleus.
